- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects in subsequent days; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 periods.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true (e.g., >5% over 3–5 days), consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often lags true trend; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 periods to catch momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising; reduce initial forecast by 1–2% to align with true trend.
